name: In-Q-Tel
identity_check: Confirmed as In-Q-Tel, Inc., brand 'IQT', at iqt.org. Its FAQ calls it a 501(c)(3) not-for-profit set up by the CIA in 1999 (first named In-Q-It on the milestones page) as an independent strategic investment firm. It invests in commercial startups whose technology serves U.S. intelligence and national-security agencies (CIA, NSA, NGA, NRO, DIA, Space Force and others) and the UK and Australian intelligence communities. It is not a government agency or part of the CIA (its own FAQ says so), and its in-house units IQT Labs and IQT Emerge are not separate investors. Not IQ Capital, a UK VC that co-invested beside IQT in RevEng.AI. Rounds were kept only where the round page names 'In-Q-Tel' or 'IQT'. Odyssey, DefendEye and HavocAI also appear in IQT's own recaps or newsletters. Skild AI's page names only 'IQT' among investors, and no IQT page lists Skild, so that match rests on the name alone.

open_items: Leads: not stated. No recorded round names IQT as lead. Bertone says IQT brings in about $40 of outside capital per dollar it commits and takes a board-observer seat on every deal, which points to co-investing, so `leads` was left out.

Check size: equity-only checks are typically $250K-$500K and technology development agreements $500K-$3M (IQT FAQ). Bertone puts equity at about $250K and directed investments at 'low single-digit millions'. check_max_usd ($3M) is the upper end of a government-directed development agreement, not a pure equity check.

Stages: 'stage-agnostic from pre-seed to growth' comes from one press Q&A (Tectonic Defense). IQT's own submission page asks for companies with 'venture backing and technology ready to launch, or already on the market', which in practice excludes very early pre-product teams.

HQ: IQT's pages list offices (Tysons, VA; Menlo Park, CA; Cambridge, MA; London; Sydney; Singapore; Munich) but never label one as headquarters. Tysons comes from Wikipedia (database) plus Tysons being listed first; the privacy policy gives no address.
Funds: IQT does not raise closed-end funds, and no page states a fund, budget or capital pool with size and date. funds is empty.

Indian founders: nothing stated. The FAQ says IQT invests in the UK, EMEA, Asia-Pacific and Canada, has never invested in a Chinese or Russian company, and is barred by federal law from a small number of countries. The submission form has a free Country field.

requires_us_entity = 'no' rests on the FAQ's international-investments answer and on non-US portfolio companies (e.g. DefendEye, datelined Krakow with a Miami unit; RevEng.AI, datelined London). No explicit entity or flip policy is published. Submissions may be shared with the CIA, the Intelligence Community and other U.S. agencies, and must not be marked proprietary or confidential.

Lead '4dev US robotics map: backed 6 makers' was not verified; the map was not fetched. IQT's portfolio categories (AI, Cyber, Energy, Enterprise, Hardware, Life Sciences, Microelectronics & Quantum, Space) have no robotics category, although its 2026 newsletters and recaps feature physical AI, autonomy and maritime robotics.
Web search was exhausted after two queries (shared session limit). Rounds came from IQT's own recaps and newsletters and from round URLs already in other cache files, each re-fetched here.

These IQT-listed or IQT-featured portfolio companies have no round page naming IQT yet: Firestorm Labs (new in the Winter 2025 recap; firestormlabs.com now redirects to an unrelated site); Vatn Systems (IQT logo in vatn.com's investor section, but neither its $60M Series A release, 2025-12-10, nor its $13M seed names IQT); Bifrost AI (Series A post 2024-10-30 names no investors); Harbinger (new in the Spring 2026 recap; its $160M Series C release, 2025-11-13, does not name IQT); EdgeCortix (Series B releases do not name IQT); ICON (Series D article, Oct 2026, names only Baillie Gifford and BlackRock); Archetype AI ($35M Series A, 2025-11-20, no IQT).

Also unconfirmed: Ent.AI ($100M mega-seed led by Decibel, per the seed list; ent.ai shows no funding news); Radiant's $300M Series D (radiantnuclear.com returned 403); BEI's ~US$20M Series B (Jul 2026, linked only from a LinkedIn post); Locus Lock, Glimpse Engineering, Xarion, Fonontech, SkySafe and Sakana AI (named as new portfolio companies, with no round page fetched).

Round details: the HavocAI round is dated to the month (Washington Technology says it was announced the Friday before 2025-10-14) and no series is named in either article. Odyssey states a $1.45B valuation without saying pre or post, and Skild AI 'over $14 billion'; both left null. The Odyssey page's metadata date (Oct 30, 2026) differs from its body date (June 17, 2026), and the body date matches IQT's June 2026 newsletter. DefendEye's amount is undisclosed and its four co-investors are listed without roles.

HQ country is not stated on the round pages for DefendEye (offices in Miami and Krakow), Mariana Minerals, Odyssey, Skild AI, VulnCheck (dateline Lexington, Mass.), RevEng.AI (dateline London) or EnCharge AI (dateline and office Santa Clara). Founding years are mostly not stated.

Team page lists only executive leadership and trustees, with no investment-team roster or sector focus. Jon Chait (Managing Partner) and Andrew Schwab (Principal) come from IQT recaps and newsletters, where they interviewed HavocAI on maritime autonomy. Their LinkedIn URLs, and Steve Bowsher's, are linked from IQT's own newsletter. Jennifer Nelson (EVP, International) oversees overseas investment but is not recorded, as no sector focus is stated.
